title: Are You Thinking Wrong About AI?
author: Dominic Salles
summary: Dominic Salles argues that schools are defaulting to a fear-and-restriction response to AI when the evidence-based response would be to teach students how to use it well. The emotional drivers of institutional AI policy — fear of cheating, fear of the unknown, fear of looking naive — are producing policies that actively prevent students from developing the AI literacy they will need. As a concrete alternative, Salles walks through how to set up NotebookLM as a free, personalised AI tutor accessible to any school in under ten minutes. He references the DfE's vision for AI-enabled personalised tutoring as evidence that institutional leadership already understands the transformative potential, and challenges school leaders to ask whether their current policies are serving students or managing adult anxiety.
points: Schools are managing adult anxiety, not student outcomes: AI restriction policies are driven by fear of cheating and institutional risk aversion, not by evidence about what serves learning.

NotebookLM is a free, practical example of AI as personalised tutor — accessible to any school in under ten minutes — that demonstrates the gap between restriction-by-default and evidence-based AI integration.

The DfE has explicitly articulated a vision of AI-enabled personalised tutoring as transformative for equity; schools whose policies actively prevent AI use are moving in the opposite direction from their own regulatory body.
AI literacy is a threshold competency: students who cannot work effectively with AI tools will be at a systematic disadvantage in higher education and employment, and the gap is already opening.
The question for school leaders is not 'how do we prevent AI misuse?' but 'what would it mean for our students to be genuinely AI-capable graduates?' Those questions produce very different policies.
quotes: Schools are not making rational decisions about AI. They are managing anxiety — their own and their institutions'. The students are paying for that anxiety management.
NotebookLM is a free AI tutor that any school can set up in ten minutes. The question is not whether we have the tools. The question is whether we have the will to use them.
The DfE already knows what AI could do for personalised learning. Schools that are banning AI are moving in the opposite direction from the regulatory body they are trying to satisfy.
Restriction-by-default is not a neutral choice. It is a choice to deprive students of tools that are already shaping the world they are entering.
